newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 1.00-3.00 cents lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 1.00-3.00 cents lower.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 3.00 cents per lb lower in the spot July contract and down 1.00 cent back months on Wednesday, but some traders expected the market to try to follow-through on Tuesday's strong gains.
"It's called down because there is no paper," said one trader. "But it will probably come in closer to unchanged after yesterday."

New York arabica futures ended sharply higher on Tuesday, boosted by speculative buying amid a smaller-than-expected increase in U.S. consumer coffee stocks in May. September closed up 9.10 cents, at 190.70, after ranging from 194.00 to 181.60. Spot July rose 12.20 cents, to 208.70, while the back months ended 6.20 to 8.50 higher.
The July/September switch widened to 18.00 cents at the close, from 14.90 cents on Monday.
On the charts, traders said 198.00-200.00 cents would present a major test of resistance for the September contract. Support was seen at 185.00 cents.
After Tuesday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell by 500 bags as of June 16, to 47,550 bags. There were 1,539 bags pending grading, the exchange said.

Also after Tuesday's close, the CSCE said it would decrease all coffee margins by $2,000, bringing the July "C" coffee margin to $10,000, the September "C" margin to $8,000 and the rest of the margins to $6,000, effective today.

On the weather front, no damaging cold is expected though early next week in Brazil's coffee belt, although recent wet weather could unfavorably impact the harvest, U.S.-based forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Wednesday.
London robusta futures were broadly higher early Wednesday, boosted by trade short-covering. At the midday break, LIFFE September rose $30 to $1,940 and spot July was $32 higher, at $1,932.
